title: By the Same Token
bodyHtml:
While sifting through some old papers in a computer science department, you come across a table of words and numbers. At first glance, it seemed as if these numbers were behaving completely...unpredictably. Here is what the table looked like:

Answer the following questions in the Answer Sheets:

G1. On your answer sheet, fill in possible values for the missing cells. For (e), (g), (h), (i), (j), and (k), you will receive more points for answers that are real English words than for ones that are not.

G2. You find one more mysterious table amongst the papers. This table shows some words in Shilha, a Berber language spoken in Morocco that is also known as Tasusiyt, along with information about their types, tokens, and English translations:

LSFAFUALUSA56male chicken
ZPSIAFLULRUQSNTFS67male chickens
QZPTLSALFUALRUSTFS68female chicken
QZPSTAILFLUSLQRUSINTFS79female chickens
AAAATTBBBBIRRRRRR55male pigeon
IIITBIIRINIII56male pigeons
TATBIRT57female pigeon
IITITBIRINI58female pigeons
AMFGUQNARS56ox (male bovine)
IFUNASN67oxen (male bovines)
ZSPTACFHUXNAVSTLQF68cow (female bovine)
TIFUNASIN79cows (female bovines)
ASHLHIY67male speaker of Shilha
ISHLATRHIYN68male speakers of Shilha
TASHLHIYT79female speaker of Shilha
TISHLHIYIN710female speakers of Shilha
QPZFIATPNDTNRTLNARTRTNR35mountain (masculine)
QZPIBXDZWRPLANTSRLYXNFS56mountains (masculine)
QPZNTIIAIPNDNILRANRNITNFS47mountain (feminine)1
QPZTFMITPDNMRLTANFRSHILYNV68mountains (feminine)

However, the file has been corrupted so that there are a bunch of extra letters in the “Shilha Word” column (the other three columns are still accurate). Your task is to remove the extra letters to return the Shilha words to their correct state. Note that, in order to achieve the correct Shilha words, you do not need to rearrange any letters. Instead, you just have to delete zero or more letters from each line, and if you choose the correct letters to delete, the letters that are left over will be in the correct order to spell the correct Shilha words.

1 The word defined here as “mountain (feminine)” would typically be used to mean “small mountain” rather than “female mountain,” but for consistency we have used the definition “mountain (feminine).”

Once you have figured it out, write the Shilha translations of the following English phrases on your answer sheet:

  • (l) female pigeon
  • (m) male pigeon
  • (n) cow (female bovine)
  • (o) mountain (masculine)
  • (p) mountains (feminine)

questions.partPrompt: Fill in possible values for the missing cells of the first table. For the word cells (e), (g), (h), (i), (j) and (k) you get more credit for real English words than for made-up letter strings.

questions.promptHtml: (e) A word whose Tokens count is 1
(f) Types for the word you wrote in (e)
(g) A word with 3 Types and 3 Tokens
(h) A word with 8 Types and 8 Tokens
(i) A word with 2 Types and 4 Tokens
(j) A word with 4 Types and 7 Tokens
(k) A word with 13 Types and 13 Tokens

questions.partPrompt: Write the correct (uncorrupted) Shilha translation of each English phrase.

hints.text: Ignore the meanings of the English words in the first table and just count letters. Compare rock (4 and 4) with add (2 and 3): which count changes when a letter is repeated?

Tokens counts every letter in the word (its length); Types counts only the different letters that appear at least once. In the Shilha table the Tokens number therefore tells you exactly how long the correct word is, and the Types number tells you how many distinct letters it may contain — powerful clues when you decide which letters of a corrupted string to delete. Also compare rows: the four forms of each noun differ only in their beginning and ending.

Try the very first Shilha row: LSFAFUALUSA must shrink to a 6-letter word with 5 distinct letters, and you may only delete letters, never reorder them. Deleting the L, S, and the A after F, plus the extra A and L, leaves AFULUS: six letters, with only U repeated, so 5 types and 6 tokens — a match. Notice that the plural and feminine rows for the same animal reuse those same letters with an added I, T, N, and so on.

explanationHtml:
What “types” and “tokens” mean

These are two ways of counting things. Tokens means every single item, counted one by one. Types means the number of different items. For letters in a word: tokens = how many letters long the word is; types = how many distinct letters appear in it.

Check this against the given rows:

  • rock: 4 letters, all different, so 4 types and 4 tokens.
  • add: 3 letters (a, d, d), but only 2 different ones, so 2 types and 3 tokens.
  • senselessness: 13 letters long, and the only letters used are s, e, n, l, so 4 types and 13 tokens.
  • assesses: 8 letters, using a, s, e, so 3 types and 8 tokens.

Every row in the table obeys this, so the numbers were not “unpredictable” at all.

G1: filling the gaps

For a word that is given, just count. Write out hemidemisemiquaver letter by letter (h-e-m-i-d-e-m-i-s-e-m-i-q-u-a-v-e-r) to get the token count, then list the distinct letters (h, e, m, i, d, s, q, u, a, v, r) to get the type count.

For a row where the word is missing, you invent any word that fits the numbers. Two rules follow from the definitions:

  • Types can never be bigger than tokens.
  • If types equals tokens, no letter may repeat; if tokens is bigger, some letters repeat exactly as many times as the difference requires.

So a row asking for 2 types and 4 tokens needs a four-letter word built out of just two letters, like deed or peep. A row asking for 8 types and 8 tokens needs an eight-letter word with no letter used twice, like birthday. The 13-and-13 row is the hard one: a thirteen-letter word with thirteen different letters. The introduction quietly hands you one when it says the numbers behaved “unpredictably”.

G2: undoing the corruption

Now the numbers become a tool instead of a puzzle. For each corrupted string you may only delete letters, keeping the survivors in order. The tokens column tells you exactly how many letters must survive, and the types column tells you how many of them are distinct.

Take AAAATTBBBBIRRRRRR, glossed “male pigeon”, with 5 types and 5 tokens. So the real word is five letters long with no repeats. The available letters, in order, are A, T, B, I, R — pick one of each and the answer falls out. Its partner row IIITBIIRINIII (“male pigeons”) needs six letters with five types, so exactly one letter appears twice, and only I is available more than once.

The Shilha pattern

Once several rows are recovered, a neat morphology appears. Take the “chicken” family: AFULUS “male chicken”, IFULUSN “male chickens”, TAFULUST “female chicken”, TIFULUSIN “female chickens”. The stem stays put, and:

  • masculine singular: A- in front;
  • masculine plural: I- in front and -N at the end;
  • feminine singular: T- ... -T wrapped around the masculine singular;
  • feminine plural: TI- in front and -IN at the end.

The “bovine” and “mountain” families work the same way, so each recovered word confirms three others. In the mountain family the stem itself loses its vowel in some forms (the masculine singular has an extra A that the plural and feminine forms drop), which is exactly why the types and tokens counts differ from row to row — and why those counts are the safest guide when you decide which letters to delete.

Checking your answers

Always re-count. A candidate word is only right if its length matches the tokens column, its number of distinct letters matches the types column, and its letters appear in the corrupted string in that same order.
_reviewNotes: No figures; assets empty. All keys taken from the official solution pages. G1 word cells (e), (g), (h), (i), (j), (k) are open-ended: the solution prints a, dog, speaking, noon, singing, unpredictably as examples only, so these are graded llm with the official examples as answerKey and other correct words listed as variants (official rubric: full credit for real English words, half credit for nonsense strings meeting the counts). Please verify the long corrupted Shilha strings letter by letter against the booklet, especially QPZNTIIAIPNDNILRANRNITNFS and QPZTFMITPDNMRLTANFRSHILYNV. Points were distributed evenly (G1 = 5, G2 = 5); the solution gives no per-cell breakdown.

_parkReasons.b: a (any one-letter string works; the official solution gives a, and notes I is also fine)
dog (any three-letter string with three different letters, e.g. cat, dog, abc)
speaking (any eight-letter string with eight different letters)
noon (any four-letter string using exactly two different letters)
singing (any seven-letter string using exactly four different letters; abcdbbb also counts, for half credit)
unpredictably (any thirteen-letter string with no repeated letter; troublemaking also works)
